Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Westridge?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 10 houses and 5 condos and townhomes listed in Westridge. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Westridge a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 10% (a buyers’ market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Westridge from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 3 houses and 1 condos and townhomes sold in Westridge over those 4 months; detached houses peaked in July with 2 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in June with 1 sold.

faq.q: How big is Westridge compared with the rest of Burnaby?
faq.a: In September 2026, Westridge held 2.2% of the 458 detached houses listed in Burnaby and 0.4% of the 1,333 condos and townhomes listed in Burnaby.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Westridge?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses made up 66.7% of the 15 homes listed in Westridge and condos and townhomes made up 33.3%; of the 1 that sold, houses were 100.0% and condos and townhomes 0.0%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Westridge than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses was little changed, 10 in June and 10 in September 2026 (+0.0%); condos and townhomes was 1 in June and 5 in September 2026, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall.
